versions.localizedDescription:
### Added
- **Your account on this device**: the first time you sign in on a device, the app asks once what to do with what is already there: whether one of your local players is you (that player then becomes your account's player, with its games and decks, under your account name), whether to move the cards you scanned to your account, and whether to upload your games from now on. Each question only appears when it applies, and all of them can be answered later in Settings
- **Games you played before signing up stay visible**: signed in, History → Record has a section *Only on this device* with the games this device recorded and never uploaded

### Changed
- **Match upload only sends games you finish from now on**: switching it on no longer sends every game since the app was installed. Settings says how many earlier games stay on this device
- **History says plainly where each game is**: *Only here*, *Not uploaded yet*, *Uploading*, *Uploaded* or *Upload failed*; a game another player logged with you in it says *Shared*, or *Confirm?* while it waits for your answer
- **Your games count for you on the website whatever deck you played**: the upload marks your own seat, so a deck typed in at the table, or one you deleted later, no longer leaves the game out of your record (needs ManaVoid-Web 3.338.0)
- **Deck records are per player**: your "Atraxa" and a friend's "Atraxa" are two records, in the seat picker and on the Record page
- **Deleting a player says how many of their games stay in History**

### Fixed
- **The menu mark at the centre of the board sits on whole pixels**: in a desktop window of an odd size it was drawn half a pixel off, which made it look soft

### Added
- **Cards that say you can't lose the game** (Platinum Angel, Phyrexian Unlife, Lich's Mastery and the like): when a player is knocked out by life, poison or commander damage, their tile offers *Can't lose* until the next action. Tap it and they stay in with the damage kept, the turn comes back if it had been passed on, and from then on nothing knocks them out automatically: life can go below 0, and 10 poison or 21 commander damage don't eliminate. A badge on the tile ends the effect, and says first whether that eliminates them. The life graph after the game now goes below 0 too
- **Undo several steps in a row, and redo**: *Undo / redo* in the game menu stays open, says what the next undo would take back and what a redo would bring back, and updates after each tap. Redo is offered until you record something new. On a computer, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z (Cmd on a Mac) do the same

### Fixed
- **Undo takes back the last game action after a pause**: the first two undos after pausing, or after reopening a saved game, used to remove the pause instead and change nothing you could see

### Added
- **Your own record in History → Record**: across every game on your account, how many you played, your record and win rate against what your table sizes would give, your last ten results and current streak, how long a game typically runs and how the last 30 days compare. It is worked out on your phone from your whole match history, so it shows offline too
- **How you went out, and where you finished**: how often you were knocked out by commander damage, life loss, poison or a concession, how often you were still standing at the end, how many players you knocked out, and your finishing places by table size. A game ended with *Declare Winner* counts everyone still in as standing
- **Commanders you face**: the commanders you meet most often, and how you do in games with each of them at the table

### Changed
- **Turn order counts only your own seat**: the win rate by place in the turn order, now grouped by table size, is yours rather than every seat's at your tables
- **Your totals count every game your seat is known in**, including games someone else logged and you confirmed, so they can be higher than before. Games where you played a deck typed in by name aren't counted, and the page says how many
- **The Record and deck pages are easier to read on the light theme**: captions and bar tracks no longer fade into the cards

### Fixed
- **The playgroup no longer lists you as your own opponent**, and no longer credits you with a win whenever an unnamed player won
- **Seats without a name are numbered by turn order**, as on the website, instead of by where they happened to be listed

### Added
- **Card type suggestions**: the common types (Creature, Instant, Land, Legendary, Kindred …) are offered under the type field in card search and the collection filter, narrowing as you type, so one tap adds one
- **Delete your account in the app**: Settings → *Delete account* erases your ManaVoid account after you confirm with your password, as on the website. Games and cards saved only on this device stay on it
- **Copy a precon to your decks, or add it to your collection**, from the precon's page in Explore when you are signed in. Each asks first, naming the precon, or how many cards go into which binder. A copied precon is ready to pick for a seat
- **Change a wishlist card's printing**: swipe a wishlist row to the right and pick another printing or finish. Needs ManaVoid-Web 3.313.0 or newer
- **Add scanned cards to your wishlist**: in a scan session, ⋮ → *Select cards* (or long-press a row), pick cards and *Add to wishlist*. It asks first, and a card already on your wishlist is raised to the number scanned rather than doubled. The cards leave the session afterwards unless you untick that, so a friend's binder never ends up in your collection by mistake
- **Scan a deck into your account**: in a scan session, ⋮ → *Save as deck* makes a deck on your account from the scanned cards. Pick the format, the commander (only scanned cards that can be one) and an optional partner, count the basic lands instead of scanning them, and optionally add the cards to your collection too. The deck is ready to pick for a seat straight away. Nothing is saved if the cards cannot all be added
- **The card sheet says what you have of a card**, as the website does: how many you own and how many of them are this printing, whether it is on your wishlist, which of your decks play it, every printing (yours marked), the cheapest printing, and *Share image*. What the phone holds shows offline. The scanner's receipt shows a small *×3* when you already own the card and a heart when it is on your wishlist
- **Add a friend at the table**: after you scan someone's Player Card into a seat, the app offers to send them a friend request, and asks before it sends it. Only offered when you're signed in and not already friends
- **Answer friend requests in the app**: requests appear at the top of Notifications, by name, with *Accept* and *Decline*, each confirmed first
- **Propose a trade in the app**: under Trades → Matches, tap a friend below a card to start a trade with them about it. Add more from their cards on your wishlist and from your own collection, set how many, and confirm before it is sent. If a copy is in one of your decks, the app says so and lets you trade anyway
- **Change the cards of an open trade, or answer a declined one with a counter-offer**: *Change cards* adds or removes cards on either side, each change confirmed as a new offer the other person has to accept again
- **Rulings on the card sheet**: the official rulings for a card, folded under *Rulings (n)* below its legality. They come through the ManaVoid website, so Scryfall never sees you, and are in English only
- **Look up a card during a game**: the game menu opens card search over the board, and back returns to the same game, without leaving or pausing it
- **Report a deck or a trade**: a community deck's menu and a trade's menu open the website's report form with the deck or trade already filled in. Not offered on your own decks or on official precons
- **Sort community decks by their minimum value**, the deck bought at its cheapest printings. Needs ManaVoid-Web 3.331.0 or newer

### Changed
- **A refused trade says why**: not friends any more, trades switched off, or twenty open trades on either side, instead of one general message. Needs ManaVoid-Web 3.334.0
- **The printings list shows each set's symbol**. Needs ManaVoid-Web 3.334.0
- **Starting a trade for a card you want no longer looks the friend's copy up first**: the match already names it. Needs ManaVoid-Web 3.334.0; older servers still work the old way
- **Your 60-card decks from the website** (Standard, Modern, Pauper) show their format in the seat's deck list and their card art, instead of passing for a Commander deck without a picture
- **The deck browser's format filter offers Pauper instead of Legacy**, the four formats a ManaVoid deck can have
- **Adding a card to your wishlist from the card sheet can be undone**: a message says it was added, with *Undo*. Undo takes back only that copy, so a card already on your wishlist keeps the copies it had

### Fixed
- **Signing in on a slow connection can no longer end your session on every device**: when several requests needed a fresh login at once, each sent the same one-time token, which the website treats as a stolen copy. They now share one renewal

### Added
- **Search for several card types at once**: add types as chips and match all of them ("Artifact" and "Creature") or any of them, in card search and the collection filter, like rules text

### Changed
- **Card rows in search, set pages and decks show set and number on a line of their own**, so a long type line no longer cuts them off
- **The colour filter is the six mana symbols across the full width**, grey until picked and in their own colour once picked, colourless included, in every card, deck and precon filter. The colour count sits right under the colours instead of behind *More filters*
- **Rarity is picked from the website's rarity pills**, and uncommon is silver on the phone and the website, no longer the same grey as common. German keeps the English rarity names, as German players, the cards and the website do
- **A collection row shows what it is worth**: the row's total, and the count times one copy's price under it, as on the website. The collection's total value is in bold
- **Foil and etched cards are marked the website's way**, a rainbow or gold stripe down the row's edge, in the collection, the wishlist and trades, instead of a sparkle (which also marked etched cards as foil on the wishlist)

### Fixed
- **Card thumbnails in lists are sharp**: search results, set pages, decks, the wishlist, trades, the scan receipt and the printing picker decoded each image at its exact size on screen, which blurred it
- **Mana symbols are sharp** at small sizes, and so is the Cardmarket button on the card sheet
- **Etched cards are valued at their etched price** in the collection, scan sessions, decks, the card sheet and the CSV export, instead of the foil or (usually) the plain printing's price
- **Foil-only and etched-only printings show a price** in card search and on set pages, labelled with the finish (a serialized or showcase card used to show none)
- **"Got them" in the wishlist's selection bar is no longer cut to "Got…"** while half the bar is empty

### Added
- **Choose the scanner's text recognition** in Settings → Text recognition: Google ML Kit, or an engine that sends nothing anywhere: Tesseract on Android, Apple's Vision on iOS. The local engine opens the scanner without the ML Kit consent question. Offered side by side while the two are compared

### Changed
- **The scan receipt shows the card's name on a line of its own**, with set, number and price below and the confidence on the right, at a fixed width that no longer jumps with the name. The session's value sits centred at the top
- **The scanner finds more cards' outlines**: borderless and pale cards on a pale table, whose edge it used to miss, so their set code and collector number are read too
- **Older cards get the right printing**: a card that prints a collector number but no set code (roughly 1998–2014) is matched to the printing with that number, instead of the newest printing of the card
- **The card's own language is read off it** (`SET DE`) even when the dot between set code and language is not recognised, so a German card is compared with its German name on any phone
- **A capture is corrected when the scanner reads the card better a moment later**, instead of keeping the first, weaker guess at its printing
- **Cards with the title in the middle** (the inverted borderless frame) are recognised by name

### Fixed
- **A card was added twice when you placed the next one**: the first reading of the new card was taken for the old card. A card lying still is also no longer added again after a moment without a readable title

### Added
- **Swipe a card in your collection**: right to edit it, left to remove it. A removal waits for its Undo to run out, so taking it back means the card was never removed. Swipe a wishlist card left to remove it, with Undo
- **Change a card's printing** from its Edit dialog: every printing of the card in a grid, one picture each with its finishes and their prices underneath, the current printing first. Sort by release date or price, either way round; the app remembers your choice
- **Search, sort and filter precons** in Explore: search by deck or commander name, sort by release date, name or value, and filter by product type, set and colour identity in the same filter sheet the community decks use (needs the matching website update)
- **Price change on the card sheet**: how much the price moved over the selected range, in money and per cent, next to "Price history"

### Changed
- **A much shorter Licences page.** Settings → Licences now groups the open-source components by licence (Apache 2.0, MIT, BSD and so on) in a few collapsible sections instead of listing some 550 entries one by one. Every component and its full licence text is still there, one tap away
- **A tidier card sheet**: the mana cost sits on the name's line, the details are one compact panel (set, rarity, language, quantity, condition, finish, origin, when it was added, mana value, artist and more), and the buy buttons show TCGplayer's and Cardmarket's logos instead of cut-off text
- **"Correct" is now "Edit"**, and the dialog lists conditions from worst to best and offers only the finishes the printing actually has. Every other condition picker reads worst to best too
- **Sharper mana symbols** everywhere: they were drawn from a shrunken copy of the artwork and looked grainy
- **Sharper deck and precon pictures** in Explore: the commander art was decoded too small for its square and blown up
- **Settings footer**: Privacy policy, Terms of Service, Impressum and Licences sit together in one compact row, and the privacy note now says what actually leaves the phone: camera pictures never do, the recognised card details go to ManaVoid, and Google ML Kit receives usage data only if you agree. The scanner switches are hidden on desktop, where there is no scanner
- **"Delete local players and decks"** says what it does: it removes players and decks created on this device and keeps your account's player and decks, your games and your collection
- The selected binder's chip no longer repeats the card count shown right under it
- The filter sheet for community decks has clearly separated sections, with the bracket and colour buttons centred
- Precon rows drop "100 cards" for Commander decks, where it is always 100

### Fixed
- The **Later** and **Review** buttons on the Terms notice were almost invisible against the notice
- Sets showed "1 cards"
- The wishlist's card sheet offered "Add to wishlist" for a card already on it, which added another copy
- Wishlist rows loaded the full-size card image for a small thumbnail

### Added
- **"Check your inbox" until your email address is confirmed.** When the website asks a signed-in account to confirm its address first, the app shows which address the link went to, resends the email, lets you continue once you have clicked the link, and opens the website to change a wrong address. You stay signed in and nothing on the phone is cleared; the account just does not sync until the address is confirmed
- **Act on several wishlist cards at once.** Tap **Select** (or long-press a card), tick cards or **Select all**, then:
  - **Got them** moves them into your collection and off your wishlist: pick a binder (or none), one condition and the date you got them, and how many of each arrived — fewer than you wished for leaves the rest on the wishlist. Cards are added in the printing on your wishlist; change the printing afterwards on the website
  - **Buy** gives the shopping list as names only or with set, to copy, open in TCGplayer's Mass Entry, or paste into a Cardmarket Wants list
  - **Remove** takes them off your wishlist, after asking
  - **Use cheapest printing** (under ⋮) switches them to the cheapest printing of each card, after asking; cards without a price stay as they are
  - Got them, Remove and Use cheapest printing need a connection and say so when you are offline; against a website that does not offer them yet, they say that instead of failing

### Added
- **Explore → Precons.** The official preconstructed decks the website lists, filtered by type (Commander decks first) and by set, newest first. Each opens with its full list, the set it shipped in and its release date; share and "open on web" go to the precon's page on the website
- **Collection & Wishlist.** Signed in, the collection screen switches between your collection and your wishlist, instead of hiding the wishlist behind a bookmark icon
- **Trade matches show one side at a time**: a switch under Matches flips between **You want** (cards friends have that are on your wishlist) and **They want** (your cards on friends' wishlists), each with its count
- **The scanner shows what the session is worth** at the top, between Close and the torch: the running total of every card scanned so far, in your currency

### Fixed
- **A foil card in a deck list shows its foil price.** Deck lists priced every card as non-foil, so a card that ships foil (a precon's commander) showed no price while the deck's total counted it
- **A trade with someone who deleted their account says "Deleted account"** in your language, and no longer offers a message box the server would refuse
- **Traded cards name their printing** as set and collector number, as on the website
- **The scan session lists the card you just scanned first**, including a second copy of a card already in it, which brings its row back to the top. Scan order, price and confidence sorted the opposite way to their arrow, so the default showed the oldest scan on top and "descending" price the cheapest card

### Added
- **Settings links the Terms of Service and the Impressum**, beside the privacy policy and the Licences, each opening on the website
- **New Terms can be accepted before they take effect.** While a change to the Terms is announced, the home screen says from when it applies; "Review" shows what changes, links the changes and the full text on the website, and accepts them now (with the age confirmation when the new Terms ask for it), so the Terms screen does not stop you on the day. "Later" hides the notice for that version on this phone

### Changed
- **Deck lists group double-faced cards by their front face**, as the website does: Agadeem's Awakening is a sorcery, a Pathway a land, an Ixalan flip land an enchantment. The Lands heading says **+N MDFC** when the deck also holds modal double-faced spells that can be played as a land (maybeboard not counted)
- **The privacy policy opens in the app's language**: the German Datenschutzerklärung for German, its English translation otherwise — from Settings and from the ML Kit consent dialog
- **"Create account" opens the registration form** instead of the website's front page
- **New Terms no longer look like a lost session.** From 3 November the website refuses an account's requests until new Terms are accepted; the app now brings up the Terms screen when that happens, and never signs you out over it

### Fixed
- **A session that expired while you were away no longer leaves your account's data on the phone.** Signing out cleared your decks, collection, match history and wishlist from the phone, but a session that had run out by the next launch only removed the sign-in, so all of it stayed — visible while signed out, and to the next account signed in here. Both now clear the same things

### Added
- **Settings → Licences.** Every open-source package in the app with its licence text, plus the three bundled fonts (SIL Open Font License) and the Manamoji symbols, and on Android the native libraries the scanner and QR reader link — Google ML Kit, Play Services, AndroidX, TensorFlow Lite. The native list is regenerated with `tool/update_native_licenses.sh`
- **The Terms screen can ask you to confirm you are at least 16**, when a new version of the Terms asks every account to (the next one will). The Accept button waits for the box
- **A suspended account sees why.** If your account is suspended, the app shows the reasons, the basis and how long it lasts instead of the app, says how to contest it, and offers exporting your data or deleting your account on the website, or signing out. Your games on the phone are not affected, and a game in progress is not interrupted

### Removed
- **The scanner no longer falls back to Scryfall, and no longer asks for consent.** The app now contacts nobody but ManaVoid. If ManaVoid's card lookup can't be reached, Scan Cards says so and asks you to try again later. The "Scanner: card lookup via Scryfall" switch in Settings is gone with it

### Changed
- **Explore → Sets shows the symbol of every set that has one.** Secret Lair, The List, promo and token sets were drawn with a placeholder, because their symbol is filed under a different name than the set's code — about 560 of the sets in the list
- **The scanner identifies cards through ManaVoid, not Scryfall.** Card names, set codes and collector numbers are looked up on manavoid.app, so scanning no longer sends anything to the USA and no longer asks for consent. It also reads damaged text better — a misread like "Lightn1ng B0lt" is still found — and cards in other languages arrive with their prices straight away. Scryfall is asked only if ManaVoid's lookup is ever unavailable, and then only after you agree, exactly as before

### Changed
- **Card images and set symbols now load from manavoid.app** instead of straight from Scryfall in the USA, so your IP address no longer goes to Scryfall when a card is drawn. The pictures are the same
- **The scanner asks before it looks cards up at Scryfall.** Identifying a card still means sending the text the scanner reads, and your IP address, to Scryfall in the USA, and that now needs your consent the first time you open Scan Cards. You can withdraw it in Settings at any time
- **The scanner gets its list of set codes from ManaVoid** rather than from Scryfall

### Fixed
- **The scanner keeps to Scryfall's request limits.** It could send up to ten name lookups a second where Scryfall allows two, and after being told to slow down it now pauses for the 30 seconds Scryfall asks for instead of carrying on

### ⚠️ Upgrade note
- **Coming from 0.40.0, the app starts with empty on-device data.** Its database file was renamed in 0.40.1, which was never published, so this is the first release that carries the change. Your game log, the players you created and any cards you scanned without being signed in stay behind in the old file, which is left untouched rather than deleted. Everything in your account — decks, collection, binders, wishlist, trades, match history — comes straight back down when you sign in
- **Needs the current ManaVoid website** (3.251.0 or newer, which is what manavoid.app runs). Against an older server the collection says so and keeps the copy it has

### Changed
- **The collection's filter has every filter card search has**: type, rules text, mana value, format legality, power and toughness, rarity, price, and under *More filters* sets, keyword, mana cost, colour count, loyalty and artist — as well as its own condition, finish and colours. The sets and artists offered are the ones in your collection, it all works offline, and it still applies as you change it. Colours now offer the same five match modes as search, replacing the separate "colour identity" checkbox. For cards from your account the new filters need the website's latest update and fill in on the next refresh
- **The collection's total value is shown in full** — `€7 712` rather than `€7.7k`, for all cards and for each binder. Totals under a thousand keep their cents
- **Card search filters are ordered by what you reach for**: colours, type, rules text, mana value, format, then power and toughness — now side by side on one line — with rarity and price after. Sets moved under *More filters* with keyword, mana cost, colour count, loyalty and artist
- **Explore → Decks and Explore → Sets draw a faint line between rows**, so one entry no longer runs into the next
- **The player card is shorter and tidier**: the explanation under the code is two sentences instead of four, and getting a new card is a refresh icon beside "Valid until" rather than a line of its own
- **The light theme shows the full-colour ManaVoid mark** on the home screen, the same one as the dark theme, instead of a plain outline

### Fixed
- **A busy server no longer shows up as an error.** When the website is under load it now asks the app to come back in a moment; the app waits the few seconds it asks for and tries again, up to four times, instead of reporting a failure — and a collection sync that meets it partway carries on from where it was rather than starting over. Adding cards is never retried this way, so a busy moment can never double them
- **Signing out while your account's data was still loading no longer leaves it behind.** A refresh already running — of your collection, decks, match history, wishlist or player card — could finish after you signed out and write that data back, where it stayed visible, and visible to the next account signed in on the same phone. Signing out now waits for anything still loading, then clears
- **Your account's collection now only downloads what changed.** The first time, it comes down whole, in our tests about 10 seconds for a 24,000-entry collection that used to take over two minutes. After that, a refresh brings only the cards added, edited, moved or removed since the last one, and takes a fraction of a second. Prices and **format legality** are updated once a day, so a card banned in Commander shows as banned the day after, even offline. The whole collection is still fetched afresh once a week, for corrected rules text and new images
- **Large collections from your account load completely.** The download no longer stops after 25,000 entries, and entries that arrived twice are kept once. Refreshes that overlap — opening the app, pulling to refresh and editing a card at once — no longer each download the whole collection. If the ManaVoid server were ever older than this app needs, the collection now says so and keeps the copy it has, instead of quietly falling back to a slow full download
- **Settings no longer says the player names you type are uploaded with a game.** They have not been since the upload stopped publishing anybody's name; the description now says they stay on your phone
- **Switches that are off are visible again.** In both themes an off switch was drawn in almost exactly the colour of its own track — most noticeably *Upload match history* in Settings, which looked like an empty patch rather than a control
- **The *Upload match history* block in Settings lines up with the rest of the page**: its rows are highlighted to the edge of the card like every other block, and its title sits on the same line as the ones below it
- **The player card's QR code is sharp.** Its squares were drawn at slightly different widths and overlapped by half a pixel, which made the code look ragged; every square is now an exact block of screen pixels
- **Deck portraits are sharp, with smooth round edges** — on the player card and in the seat picker. The commander art was being loaded too small and stretched to fill the circle, and the circle's edge was jagged
- **The notification, trade and player-card buttons sit at the right edge of the home screen in landscape** rather than partway across the header

### Performance
Measured the same way before and after: the app's own sync code against the live server, signed in as a 24,216-entry test account, on a desktop; three refreshes in a row over an existing copy.
- **First sync of your account's collection: 134 s → 10 s.** It comes down through the new sync feed in 13 requests instead of 49, and saving it on the device went from ~96 s to about 1 s
- **Every refresh after that: 134 s → 0.24–0.41 s**, because only what changed is sent. An edit made on the website arrived in 0.24 s
- **The daily price and legality update: 1.9 s**, for 19,531 cards
- **Entries received: 24,216 of 24,216** (before the server fix of the same day, 1,848 were missing)
- Peak memory of the test process during a sync: 608 MB (desktop, including the test harness; no earlier figure to compare against)

### Changed
- **The app is now called ManaVoid**, with the new mark on the home screen and as its icon on every platform. The website was renamed at the same time and now lives at **manavoid.app**; nothing about your games, decks or collection changes because of the name
- **The app now talks to manavoid.app.** The old address still answers, so signing in, your decks, your collection and your match history are unaffected either way. "Create an account" now opens the same site the app is signed in to rather than a hardcoded one
- **The game menu opens from the mark at the centre of the table**, in place of the black circle with three lines in it. Same tap, same menu, and it reads the same way up from either side of the table

### Fixed
- **The poison icon sat slightly off-centre in its circle on the far side of the table.** It happened on every tile across from you *except* whoever's turn it was, which is what made it look like a quirk of the active tile rather than a bug. The active tile's border is thicker, and the border was shifting everything on the tile by a pixel and a half — harmless on your own side, but the far row is drawn upside down, which turned that shift into exactly half a pixel and split the glyph across two rows of pixels. The border no longer moves anything, so the whole tile now also stops twitching as the turn passes

### ⚠️ Upgrade note
- **This installs as a new app rather than replacing the old one.** ManaVoid carries new platform identifiers, which is what lets the two exist side by side — and is also why **nothing is carried across**: your game log, players, decks, collection and binders stay in the ManaVortex app, which keeps working and which you should not delete until you are sure you have what you need. Anything in your account (decks, collection, binders, wishlist, trades, match history) comes straight back down when you sign in, because it never lived on the phone. What is **only** on the phone is the game log, the players you created, and any cards you scanned without being signed in — sign in and use Collection → *Move these cards to my account* before switching if you want the last of those to come with you
